label: sec:algebraic-substrate-intro
html:
The algebraic substrate is the Frobenius--Hopf algebra A viewed as a graded ring equipped with the Reeb derivation—the differential operator forced by the categorical volume constraint. We develop the algebraic programme: substrate structure and Reeb derivation, the unit particle as a categorical invariant, spectral trace and Tannaka--Krein duality, geometric stability via the Hasse--Weil bound, and the classical limit recovering the macroscopic continuum.

The spectral trace formula relates the q-zeta function of A to the Chebyshev function of the Reeb flow. A stability criterion derives from the Weil bound on the fibre geometry. The classical limit q \to 1 emerges as a functor that fails to be an equivalence, with the obstruction to classicality acting as a non-trivial categorical invariant.
